metadata.title: Combined Food and Drug Administration and Sponsor Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee Briefing Document
metadata.topic: Draft guideline · FDA human drugs and biologics
metadata.legal_basis: FDA Guidance Document (21 CFR 10.115). Guidance states FDA's current thinking and is not binding unless a statute or regulation requires it; the official text governs.

metadata_verification: Source-register metadata; dates and legal status require human verification.
limitations: English rule-based extraction; no GPT or paid API.

candidates.statement: In general, FDA’s guidance documents do not establish legally enforceable responsibilities. 25 Instead, guidances describe the Agency’s current thinking on a topic and should be viewed only 26 as recommendations, unless specific regulatory or statutory requirements are cited. The use of 27 the word should in Agency guidances means that something is suggested or recommended, but 28 not required. 29
candidates.context: This guidance provides recommendations to Sponsors regarding use and development of a 15 combined version of the briefing document for matters before the Oncologic Drug Advisory 16 Committee (ODAC), as part of the Oncology Center of Excellence’s (OCE) Project 17 Point/Counterpoint initiative. This single briefing document includes information that 18 customarily would be contained in separate briefing documents prepared individually by the 19 Sponsor and by FDA. 2 Project Point/Counterpoint is an option for advisory committee meetings 20 for oncology products. Sponsors in non-oncology therapeutic areas who want to discuss whether 21 a combined advisory committee briefing document may be appropriate for their applications 22 should contact the relevant FDA review division. 23

candidates.statement: Consistent with FDA’s 2008 Guidance, Sponsors and FDA customarily prepare separate ODAC 33 briefing documents. 3 This can lead to repetition of information (i.e., trial design, endpoints, 34 eligibility criteria, etc.) and increases the number of documents that ODAC committee members 35 need to review. Additionally, ODAC committee members may need to go back and forth from 36 each briefing document to consider the Sponsor’s and FDA’s position on each issue. Project 37
candidates.context: 1 This guidance has been prepared by the Oncology Center of Excellence (OCE), the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research (CDER), and the Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research (CBER) at the Food and Drug Administration.

candidates.statement: • Sponsors should inform FDA of their interest in using Point/Counterpoint early on in the 48 ODAC process, ideally at the first discussion with FDA about ODAC planning. 49
candidates.context: III. PROCESS & RECOMMENDATIONS 46 • FDA provides Sponsors who have expressed an interest in using the combined briefing 51 document with a blank Project Point/Counterpoint combined briefing document template 52 within 2 weeks of making a determination that a product will be discussed at ODAC. 53 Sponsors are informed that an ODAC is planned as soon as possible after the submission 54 of an application, perhaps even before receipt of the application, especially for priority 55 reviews. For standard reviews, Sponsors are informed that an ODAC is planned no later 56 than the filing meeting. 57

candidates.statement: • The Sponsor completes their sections in the combined briefing document template, 59 explaining their positions. The Sponsor’s sections including tables and figures, should not 60 exceed 35 pages. Any additional appendices may not exceed 20 pages in total. 61 Formatting details (e.g., margins, font type, font size, etc.) should meet 508 compliance 62 standards. The Sponsor should submit the combined briefing document template in both 63 PDF and .docx formats. 64
